<reason>B wins by defending an open default while directly accommodating legitimate privacy, rights, and commercialization constraints. A identifies genuine risks to exclusivity and integrated projects, but never adequately explains why advance, project-wide exceptions would fail. Its repeated prediction that partners would refuse participation remains insufficiently supported. B makes the decisive comparison clearer: both policies assess whether restrictions are necessary, but only B guarantees reuse rights when no sufficient reason for restriction exists. A’s publication-and-deposit alternative leaves that benefit unanswered.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B directly answers A’s commercialization pressure by protecting necessary exclusivity before funding or release, including across integrated projects. B then uses A’s concession that restrictive needs must be real to expose the comparative weakness: A counts justification as collaboration-killing under openness without establishing why its own assessment avoids that burden.</best_rebuttal>
